customUiPage.emptyHint: Create a component folder (for example, my-card) in the directory below with manifest.json (runtime: native) and component.js, or ask an agent to generate one with component_create. Native components run in the app’s origin; declared capabilities only describe them and gate network and storage access.

studio.capExplainer: Runs natively: same origin as the app, so it can reach everything the app can. The list above records what it declares and uses through Pisper's interfaces so you can check it anytime, but it is not an isolation boundary.
studio.capUndeclared: Not declared: {list} (Pisper's interfaces won't provide them)
studio.cardTitlePlaceholder: Shows the component name when empty
studio.created: Created “{name}”. It isn't placed anywhere yet
studio.floatingPhoneHint: Floating widgets don't show on phones
studio.logsLocalEmpty: No logs yet. Anything the component writes with ctx.log and errors caught on this page show up here.
studio.newBlankHint: Creates manifest.json and component.js in the components directory. Add a description to have an agent generate it, or edit the files yourself later. It won't be placed anywhere.

overview.heading: Placed components
sessionPanel.addHint: Components placed in the session panel show up here as tabs.

agent.promptTitle: Describe it in one sentence · the agent creates or changes this component
agent.promptPlaceholder: For example: show how many tasks each project ran today and flag the failures
agent.promptHint: Runs in the component's own agent session; follow it under Running in the sidebar
agent.generateSent: The agent is generating “{name}”. Follow it under Running in the sidebar.
agent.fixSent: The agent is fixing “{name}”. Follow it under Running in the sidebar.
agent.queued: The agent is still working on “{name}”; this request is queued after it.
agent.failed: Couldn't hand this off to the agent.
agent.editWithPrompt: Generate or change with a prompt
agent.newPromptPlaceholder: Description (optional): one sentence on what it should show; the agent generates it after creation
versions.title: Versions
versions.onlyCurrent: No earlier versions yet. One is kept each time the agent writes, an import replaces it, or you roll back.
versions.restoreHint: Creates v{next} with the contents of v{n}. The current v{current} stays in the list, so you can come back to it. Properties and placements stay the same.
exporting.done: Exported {name}. The ZIP has only the component files, no properties or stored data.
importing.unsupported: This Runtime can't import components yet
importing.needsReview: Check where it came from: review the code and capabilities before trusting it. It won't run until you do.
importing.reviewFailed: Couldn't load this import. It may have been handled already.
importing.truncated: Large file: showing the first 512 KB.
importing.replaces: A component with this id ({version}) is installed. Trusting replaces it; the old contents are kept as a version you can roll back to.
importing.viewDiff: Diff against the installed version ({count} files)
importing.manifestInvalid: The manifest is invalid, so it can't be trusted.
importing.explainer: Runs natively: same origin as the app, so it can reach everything the app can. The static scan only makes things visible; obfuscated code can get past it. Only trust components whose source you know. Trusting enables it right away.
importing.replaced: Replaced {name}. The old contents are kept as a version.
scan.clean: No calls that bypass the Pisper APIs, and every host in the code is declared.
scan.summary: {danger} bypass the Pisper APIs or run dynamic code · {warn} worth a look · {hosts} undeclared hosts
scan.truncated: Too many results or files too large; showing part of them.
scan.ruleFetch: Calls fetch directly (bypasses the Pisper network proxy)
trash.title: Trash
trash.hint: Deleted components are kept for {days} days and can be restored, then cleared automatically. Legacy components moved here at startup are never cleared automatically.
trash.purgeHint: The component's files and stored data are removed for good. This can't be undone.
usage.revoked: Revoked “{capability}”: the component can no longer use it through the Pisper APIs.
